approach:
In `producer_loop` (producer.rs), after the format step, the replay and the mirror check of each pass, Athena runs the capability's routed checks on the producer's tree with the existing `run_check`, reached through `SnapExec`. A new `Athena::loop_check_failures` (run/checks.rs) does it. A failure that is not a timeout and not already failing on the job's base becomes a `CheckFailure` (name, command, exit, output tail). Each failure adds one short problem string to `problems`, which is cloned into `report_problems`, so the stored `self-check failed: …` detail names it, and at the limit it goes to the verifier as `report_gaps` (flagged, not hidden). The full command and tail go into the one existing send-back through a new `append_check_failures` in send_back.rs, chained like `append_mirror_drift`. `PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS` stays 1 and no loop is added.

Answers to the seven findings of round 1:
1. [blocker] Leak. `GIT_INDEX_FILE` is no longer in the check env. A new guard `ExposedIndex` builds the work tree's index in a temporary file with `GIT_INDEX_FILE` set only for that one `git add -A` (as `Snapshot::work_tree_tree` does, athena-git/src/snapshot.rs:210-218), saves the snapshot's own `.git/index` bytes, copies the temporary index over it, and writes the saved bytes back on drop. `git ls-files` in a check then sees producer-added files, and no check process inherits the variable. The tests add a check that runs `git init`, `git add` and `git commit` in a fresh temp repo and checks `GIT_INDEX_FILE` is unset.
2. [major] Disk gate. The in-loop `SnapExec` starts with `gated = false`, so the disk gate runs before the first in-loop check, with the producer's build directory still present. `LowDisk` becomes a `producer   checks not run before the verifier: …` line, and verification, which frees the build first (mod.rs:2008-2011), judges the checks as before. The line does not start with `checks     `, because drain.rs:3180 and tests.rs:3161 assert that no such line appears.
3. [major] Other cli tests. drain.rs `per_job_worktree_a_rejected_job_leaves_neither_directory` (9631), `gate_run` (3130), the produce-dir test (3050-3112) and lifecycle.rs 55/131/471 are read and listed in dependents, each with the reason it passes unchanged. The producer still runs the whole `cargo test -p athena-cli`. It edits only a count or order assertion, only in lifecycle.rs or retry.rs. A failure in any other file goes into its report and is not edited (the scope check would send that back).
4. [minor] The pre-existing filter goes through one helper `usable_baseline(baseline, base)` in checks.rs, which applies the `base_commit == base` check and is also used at mod.rs:2127-2130.
5. [minor] The plan no longer says the in-loop run equals verification. `verifier_snapshot` restores the base's tool configuration (mod.rs:1976-1980) and the producer tree keeps its own, so the in-loop result is advisory and verification stays the verdict. D182's Tradeoff says so.
6. [minor] The in-loop run takes a slot with `SlotQueue::try_acquire` (slots.rs:172), which never waits and never enqueues. A busy slot gives `SlotWait`, which becomes the same skip line, so the doubled wait cannot occur. The existing test `a_check_that_waited_checks_the_disk_again` (tests.rs:5237) keeps its meaning, because its `wait_until_waiting(probe, 1)` only ever sees the verification-time ticket.
7. [nit] Step numbers in the demonstrations are corrected below, and the format tests are cited at run/tests.rs:468-720.

decisions.choice: Show producer-added files to `git ls-files` by building the work tree's index in a temporary file (`GIT_INDEX_FILE` set only for that one `git add -A`), copying it over the snapshot's `.git/index` for the length of the in-loop run, and restoring the saved index bytes when a guard (`ExposedIndex`) is dropped. `GIT_INDEX_FILE` is never put in the check env.
decisions.reason: A check env that holds `GIT_INDEX_FILE` leaks into every git process the checks start. `run_check` clears the env and then sets `ctx.env` (core/src/checks.rs:532-536). `Git::command` only adds variables (athena-git/src/lib.rs:233-246). So Athena's own tests, which build temp repos with git, would write one shared index whose blobs exist only in the producer's object store, and the in-loop `cargo test` would fail for no fault of the work. Swapping the index file keeps the temporary-index method of `Snapshot::work_tree_tree` and still lets `git ls-files` list new files. A drop guard covers every error path.

rejected.option: Export `GIT_INDEX_FILE` to the check processes (the previous plan)
rejected.why: Leaks into the git calls of the tests the checks run, so parallel test threads race on one index and commits fail on missing blobs.

rejected.option: Run the in-loop checks in a committed two-commit snapshot built like `verifier_snapshot`
rejected.why: The candidate commit does not exist yet inside the loop, and a second full copy of the work tree per pass costs disk and time for no gain over an index swap.

rejected.option: Run `git add -A` into the snapshot's real index and leave it
rejected.why: It leaves staged changes in the producer's repository for the next pass and for the producer's own `git status` or `git diff`.

decisions.choice: Reuse `SnapExec` for the in-loop run with one new field `in_loop: bool` (false at mod.rs:2037, true in the loop). When true, `exec` skips the test-only `check_seam` and takes a slot with `try_acquire` (error `SlotWait { waited_s: 0, limit_s: 0 }` when none is free). The run starts with `gated = false`, so the disk gate runs first.
decisions.reason: `SnapExec::exec` (run/checks.rs:98-145) gives the kill switch, the disk gate, the slot's warm target link, `run_check` and the `restore_to(prepared)` that removes check-made files from the producer tree before the change list is taken again. The seam is skipped so the seven tests that install `check_seam` (tests.rs:4521, 4959, 5023, 5252, 5590, 6390, 6788) keep one check call per check. `try_acquire` never enqueues, so there is no second wait at verification and `a_check_that_waited_checks_the_disk_again` still tests the verification-time wait.

rejected.option: Call `run_check` directly with a hand-built `CheckContext`, as `format_stage` does (producer.rs:196)
rejected.why: No disk gate, no build slot and no warm target, so `cargo test` would build cold in the producer's own target directory, and check-made files would stay in the tree.

rejected.option: Mark the in-loop run `gated = true` (the previous plan)
rejected.why: The producer's build is still on disk during the loop, and the gate is what stops a low-space build failure from being sent back as a fault in the work.

rejected.option: Wait for a slot for up to `build_wait_s`
rejected.why: It could wait twice per job (once here, once at verification) and it changes the meaning of tests.rs:5237.

decisions.choice: Run every routed, non-skipped check in config order and send back each new failure: failed, not timed out (`checks::timed_out`), and not pre-existing on the base (`verify::is_pre_existing` with `usable_baseline`). A `LowDisk` or `SlotWait` ends the run with a `producer   checks not run before the verifier: …` line and returns the failures found so far. The kill-switch error propagates.
decisions.reason: One repair pass can then fix fmt, clippy and test together, which is the goal. Verification already holds a job whose only new failures timed out (mod.rs:2144) and leaves pre-existing failures out of the verdict, so sending the producer back for either would have it chase a fault it cannot fix. The base-commit filter is the one verification applies (mod.rs:2127-2130).

rejected.option: Stop at the first failing check
rejected.why: It would spend the one send-back on the first fault only and leave the later checks to fail at verification.
It spends the send-back on timeouts and on base failures the verdict ignores.

decisions.choice: Render with `append_check_failures(text, &[CheckFailure])` in send_back.rs, chained after `append_mirror_drift` and `append_missing_changelog` at producer.rs:639. It adds a leading sentence after the last `## Sent back` heading and a closing section with each check's name, command, exit status and output tail (at most 3000 bytes each).
decisions.reason: Later send-back additions use this shape (send_back.rs:219-267). The intro of `send_back_text_scoped` speaks only of criteria, so a leading sentence is needed. The four `send_back_text*` wrappers and their callers stay unchanged.

rejected.option: Add a `checks` parameter to `send_back_text_scoped` and its three wrappers
rejected.why: It touches every wrapper and call site (producer.rs:622-638 and the send_back.rs tests) for no gain over the append pattern.

decisions.choice: Run the in-loop checks on every pass, including the second, and put a one-line summary of each failure in both `problems` and `report_problems`. Skip a nested run, a pinned run (`ctx.pin_dir`) and a pass with an empty change list. The loop never calls `ctx.stages.enter(.., Stage::Checks)`.
decisions.reason: A check still failing after the send-back must reach the verifier as flagged (criterion 2): `report_problems` becomes `report_gaps` (producer.rs:576-583), which candidate.rs:47-50 and verification.rs:100-112 already carry. Not entering `Stage::Checks` keeps the stage order that lifecycle.rs:1589 pins (Producer, Producer, Checks, Verifier). An empty change list fails as an idle producer after the loop.

rejected.option: Run only on the first pass
rejected.why: Nothing would flag a check that still fails, and a fix that breaks another check would go unseen.

decisions.choice: Do not edit docs/decision-links.toml. D182 is worded without `amends`, `supersedes` or `superseded` and says D115 and D156 stand.
decisions.reason: The only `[[governs]]` entry is D08, for athena-git/src/snapshot.rs and run/candidate.rs (decision-links.toml:219-224). Neither file is touched, so the decision gate asks for nothing, and criterion 7 asks for a link only when the entry amends or supersedes an earlier one.

rejected.why: D115 (recorded checks on the same tree count as evidence) is applied here, not revised.

risks.risk: Added wall time per job: each pass now runs fmt, clippy and the full test on the producer's tree, and verification runs them again.
risks.mitigation: The run shares the warm slot target, so third-party crates stay compiled (checks.rs:233-239); it is skipped for a nested run, a pinned run, an empty change list, low disk and a busy slot; each check keeps its `check_timeout_s` bound. Not measured: the added wall time per job. D182's Tradeoff says so.

risks.risk: The in-loop result can differ from the verification result: the producer tree keeps its own tool configuration, while `verifier_snapshot` restores the base's (mod.rs:1976-1980).
risks.mitigation: The in-loop result is advisory and verification stays the verdict (the verifier runs all checks again). A producer that weakens a tool config passes in the loop and fails at verification, as `relaxed_tool_configuration_does_not_relax_its_check` (lifecycle.rs:905) expects. D182's Tradeoff states this and no 'same as verification' claim is made.

risks.risk: A busy slot or low space skips the in-loop run, so the producer sees no early feedback in a busy drain.
risks.mitigation: Verification judges the checks as before, so only the early feedback is lost. The skip prints a `producer   checks not run before the verifier: …` line, so it is visible, and it is stated in D182.

risks.risk: The temporary index is installed over the snapshot's `.git/index` and a failure to restore it would leave staged changes.
risks.mitigation: A drop guard writes back the saved bytes (or removes the file if there was none) on every exit; `work_tree_tree` and `restore_to` do not read that index; `the_exposed_index_lists_new_files_and_is_restored_on_drop` checks the bytes after the drop.

risks.risk: A check that writes into the tree changes the candidate.
risks.mitigation: `SnapExec::exec` calls `restore_to(prepared)` after each check, with `prepared` taken just before the run, so check-made files are removed before the change list is taken again. The criterion 4 tests show the producer count stays 1.

risks.risk: Tests outside the deliverables break from the extra producer pass (drain.rs, introspection.rs, steward.rs, code_health_hooks.rs).
risks.mitigation: Each was read (see dependents) and passes by reasoning. The producer runs the full `cargo test -p athena-cli`, edits only a count or order assertion in lifecycle.rs or retry.rs, and reports a break in any other file in its report without editing it.

risks.risk: Output tails of up to three failing checks make the send-back brief long.
risks.mitigation: Each tail is cut to the last 3000 bytes with `checks::tail`, and at most the routed checks (three in Athena's own repository) are listed.

demonstrations.method: Behavior test plus a diff read. The test of criterion 3 also loads `Records` and asserts that the first producer invocation's `detail` contains `self-check failed: check probe failed before the verifier`. A unit test in send_back.rs `check_failure_tests` (`the_send_back_names_the_failed_check`) renders `append_check_failures` on a `## Sent back` brief with one `CheckFailure { name: "probe", command: "sh -c …", exit: "exit code 1", tail: "MISSING-FIXED-TXT" }`: it must contain the command, `exit code 1` and the tail, and an empty slice must return the text unchanged. A test `the_exposed_index_lists_new_files_and_is_restored_on_drop` (tests.rs) builds a snapshot with `Snapshot::create`, adds `NEW.txt`, builds the `ExposedIndex`, runs `git ls-files` (lists NEW.txt), drops it, and runs `git ls-files` again (no NEW.txt, and the saved index bytes equal the original). The diff shows the call in `producer_loop`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE` used only in the `git add -A` of `ExposedIndex::new`, and the checks run through `SnapExec` and `run_check`. The commands the verifier may also run are `cargo test -p athena-core the_send_back_names_the_failed_check`, `cargo test -p athena-core the_exposed_index_lists_new_files` and `git diff -- crates/athena-core/src/run`.
demonstrations.observes: The tests pass. The second producer brief has the check section with the command, the exit status and the tail; the first producer invocation's stored detail names `check probe failed before the verifier`; the temporary index is installed for the checks and removed after.
demonstrations.fails_without: With no in-loop run, the producer count is 1, `prompts[1]` does not exist and no `check probe failed` text is stored. With no temp-index swap, `git ls-files` would not list NEW.txt in the guard test.

Fixture: `athena_with(&repo, &state, NEEDS_FIXED_FILE, plenty_of_space, script)` (tests.rs:191), with the real `run_check` running `sh -c` (no `check_seam` installed); `NEEDS_FIXED_FILE` passes on the base and fails once the README has `A demo` and `FIXED.txt` is missing, so the base run does not make it pre-existing. `script` wraps `editing(..)` (tests.rs:3066) to add `FIXED.txt` only when the prompt has `## Sent back`, the device of `reconciling_on_send_back` (tests.rs:3120). open_questions: User: Criterion 1 says the in-loop checks run "with GIT_INDEX_FILE set to a temporary index of the work tree". This plan sets GIT_INDEX_FILE only for the one `git add -A` that builds the temporary index (as `Snapshot::work_tree_tree` does) and then installs that index as the snapshot's `.git/index` for the checks. It does not export the variable to the check processes, because a shared temporary index breaks the git calls of Athena's own tests. Is that reading of criterion 1 acceptable?
